The end-to-end funnel is ≈ 0.2% cold-inbound to offer (340–380 applications per offer for engineering); referral yield is 11–36× higher per application. The binding constraint is getting into the interview loop, not passing it

AI system design interviews bifurcate into infrastructure (41/112 Anthropic reports: inference serving, batching, GPU scheduling) and application (RAG, agents, evals). Preparing for the wrong track is the most avoidable failure mode

The 45-minute system design blueprint (5 min requirements → 4 min targeted estimate → 9 min HLD + walk → 16 min two deep dives → 7 min eval/safety/ops → 4 min wrap) is the highest-convergence framework across coaching sources, with firm-specific time variants

Behavioral "No Hire" is a near-automatic veto at Anthropic (values round) and Google (G&L). At Meta, it triggers downlevel or rejection. Three archetype failures dominate: arrogance/poor communication, failure of ownership in production incidents, and ethical/safety blind spots

AI-specific behavioral competencies cluster around four dimensions: technical pragmatism under ambiguity, cross-functional communication of probabilistic trade-offs, ownership and incident response, and responsible AI consciousness. A STAR-AI framework (Situation → Task → Action → Result with metric delta + continuous monitoring) is the scoring template

AI-enabled coding rounds (Meta spring 2026, early signal) evaluate how candidates collaborate with an AI assistant — delegating boilerplate, owning logic, catching AI hallucinations — not whether they can generate correct code unaided. Blind reliance ("vibe coding") is a strong No Hire signal

Same-tier lateral hops yield ≈ +15–25% TC; level-up hops +35–50%. The "35–50% per hop" claim fails as a general rule and describes tier-crossers only. A hop beats staying only when the premium exceeds ~25% or promotion is blocked

Private AI equity should be risk-adjusted at 0.5–0.8× for frontier labs, 0.4–0.8× for Series C–D, and 0.15–0.3× for stale-vintage unicorns before comparing to liquid RSUs. Discount rate and bust probability dominate; preference structure is second-order (−3% to −12%)

The Doody/Fearless methodology (never disclose current salary → let them make the first offer → counter 10–20% above initial → single data-backed email) is the most-cited negotiation framework, with Levels.fyi coaching cohort data showing median uplift of +21–24% (self-selected)

Negotiation coaching services (Levels.fyi, Candor, Rora) report that ~80–87% of candidates who negotiate receive positive adjustments, but the lift depends critically on competing offers — without leverage, coaching returns are marginal

An equity due-diligence checklist (fully diluted count, preference stack, last 409A, tender history, exercise window, acceleration terms) converts paper equity from a black box into a computable risk-adjusted value. Most candidates never ask these questions

Post-interview debrief protocol — capturing exact questions within 30 minutes, running a knowledge-gap audit, and iterating before the next loop — is universally recommended by coaching sources but has no controlled evidence of pass-rate improvement

Only 8–12 of the 30 persona×tier permutations represent high-volume transition corridors; the remainder are either implausible (Non-Tech → Tier 5), already-occupied (PhD at Tier 3), or require a two-stage transition that exceeds 12 months

The 12-stage funnel compresses to 5–7 active stages per persona because experienced practitioners bypass Awareness/Exploration, credentialed practitioners skip Certification, and senior pivots compress Skills + Portfolio into a single build phase

Evaluation is the universal gate across all 5 personas and all viable tiers — it appears in portfolio (Stage 5), interview execution (Stage 9–10), and onboarding (Stage 12). Each persona brings a different comparative advantage to eval work

Tax/legal structure is a one-way door that must be decided at Stage 6 (Discovery/Application), not Stage 11 (Negotiation) — the ₹75L §44ADA cliff (T0-07) and O-1A evidence-building timeline (T0-08) both require 12–18 months of preparation that cannot be retrofitted

The interview funnel bifurcates into infrastructure and application tracks (T1-03 KF2), and the correct track depends on persona×tier: Backend→Tier 3+ is infrastructure-heavy; Frontend→Tier 2 is application-heavy; PhD→Tier 4+ straddles both. Preparing for the wrong track is the most avoidable failure mode

First-90-day failure modes are persona-specific and predictable from upstream findings: role ambiguity (43% of all hires; T0-09 F3), data absence (63% of orgs; T0-09 F4), compute gating (85% delayed; T0-09 F5), and non-determinism surprise (up to 15% accuracy variance; T0-09 F6)

The freelance/fractional path (T0-18) diverges from the employment funnel at Stage 6 and requires a parallel playbook spine: network-based acquisition replaces job boards, MSA/contract structure replaces offer negotiation, and client retention replaces onboarding

Geographic arbitrage (India→US remote) at Tier 2–3 is the highest-ROI corridor but requires navigating three simultaneous regulatory regimes (Indian tax, US client onboarding, and optionally visa/relocation), each with its own timeline and cliff effects

Portfolio calibration must match the target tier: Tier 0–1 needs one evaluated end-to-end system; Tier 2–3 needs two systems with different failure surfaces plus CI-gated evals; Tier 4–5 needs published research, industry-visible contributions, and evidence meeting O-1A or equivalent standards

No longitudinal outcome data exists for any persona×tier corridor (T0-06 KF9). Every timeline in this document is a transparent model, not measured data. The playbooks are planning frameworks calibrated against the few available anchors (an 8-month frontend retrospective, Huntr's 82–108 day search medians, and vendor reference classes)
